rich_summary: This section depicts a spectacular phase of the Kurukshetra battle centered on Arjuna’s overwhelming martial skill. Celestial beings watch from the sky as Arjuna releases a dazzling celestial weapon from the Gandiva, his speed so great that no interval can be seen between nocking and releasing arrows. Chitrasena praises the duel between Arjuna and Bhishma, two nearly unmatched warriors. Arjuna cuts Bhishma’s bow and wounds him, forcing Bhishma’s charioteer to withdraw the unconscious elder. Duryodhana then attacks and wounds Arjuna, but Arjuna retaliates fiercely, slaying Vikarna’s massive elephant with a thunderbolt-like arrow and driving the Kaurava forces into panic. When Duryodhana flees, Arjuna taunts him for abandoning royal honor. Stung by the reproach, Duryodhana turns back as Karna, Bhishma, Drona, and others rush in to protect him, setting the stage for an even larger clash.

highlight_spans.why: Celestials watching from the sky frame the battle as a cosmic spectacle, emphasizing Arjuna’s near-divine skill.
The description of Arjuna’s impossible speed with the Gandiva highlights his superhuman mastery of archery.
Bhishma being struck and left leaning on his chariot pole captures a rare moment where the invincible elder is visibly overwhelmed.
Arjuna’s thunderbolt-like arrow killing the massive elephant is a vivid demonstration of his destructive battlefield power.
Arjuna’s scornful taunt as Duryodhana flees dramatizes the moral dimension of the conflict—honor, shame, and royal duty.

top_scenes.scene_text: Celestial beings including Indra watch from the heavens as Arjuna fires a radiant stream of arrows from the Gandiva that streak across the sky in a continuous blazing line.
Arjuna’s arrow strikes the gigantic war elephant between its temples, the shaft burying to the feathers as the beast collapses like a mountain split by lightning.
Arjuna, blood streaming from his forehead like a golden garland, stands defiant on his chariot while shouting a fierce challenge at the fleeing Duryodhana.
